chunks: Al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Yunus ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, what do you say regarding hunting birds in their nests and wild animals in their lairs at night, for people dislike that?' He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.أَوْكَارُ: Nests or dens (of birds or beasts)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to hunt animals in their dens or birds in their nests at night according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) rules that hunting birds in their nests and wild animals in their lairs at night is permissible (la ba'sa), clarifying that this practice does not fall under the prohibition of *ghabn* (deception) since the animals are in their natural resting places. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between mere concealment and active deception, affirming the permissibility even when the general public dislikes the method due to its efficiency.
